source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why must a course-support workflow resolve the intended section before applying a familiar repair?

options.text: A familiar symptom proves that every section has the same current problem.
options.feedback: Sections can have different current states. The workflow needs evidence about the intended target, not only a familiar symptom.

options.text: The section can be inferred from whichever course object is easiest to edit.
options.feedback: Convenience does not identify the intended target. Resolve the course and section from the report and available evidence.

options.text: The same repair could otherwise change the wrong course area.
options.feedback: A repair can be technically familiar yet affect the wrong target. Section identification is part of establishing that the authorized procedure fits.

options.text: Checking the section after a response gives the recipient stronger evidence.
options.feedback: A later check cannot justify an earlier claim about the target. Resolve the section before changing anything and verify before responding.
